result.summary: RKLB stopped at step 1: the interest-coverage rule fails (-8.64 against a minimum of 5) because of operating losses, although the company had $2,302.2 million of cash and short-term investments at 2026-06-30. The quality score is 2: ROIC was negative in all six years and diluted shares increased 7.0% in 2025, so the policy gives no required margin of safety and the company does not qualify at any price. At $68.21 (close on 2026-10-09), the reverse DCF requires year-10 revenue of $38.49 billion with an estimated 15% FCF margin, which is 51.6% growth each year from $601.8 million in 2025. The result changes if ROIC goes above 9% and free cash flow becomes positive for two years, with dilution below 2%.

steps.reason: Competence: Rocket Lab sells launch services with its Electron rocket from its own launch complex in New Zealand and from a site in the United States. It also designs and builds spacecraft, spacecraft components (solar arrays, reaction wheels, star trackers, optical systems) and on-orbit management services; at 2025-12-31 the backlog was $1,847.3 million. It develops Neutron, a medium-lift reusable rocket; the 10-K says that a tank failure in January 2026 moved the first launch to Q4 2026. Customers are governments (about 47% of 2025 revenue came from U.S. government contracts) and commercial satellite operators. The company makes money from fixed-price contracts that it recognizes over time. The competence rule passes. Survival: the interest-coverage rule fails (-8.64 against a minimum of 5) because operating income is negative. But the balance sheet is strong: cash and short-term investments were $2,302.2 million at 2026-06-30, and long-term debt was only $1.7 million at 2025-12-31. debt-due-3y is not available. Trust in the accounts: earnings-quality is not meaningful because of the losses; receivables grew slowly from $36.4 million to $39.0 million while revenue grew 38.0%; But the 10-Q shows receivables of $112.9 million at 2026-06-30; this value has a tag_conflict flag (a second XBRL tag gives a much lower value), so the fast increase must be checked in the 10-Q notes before you trust it. SBC was 11.8% of revenue. Restatement flags are only on the 2020 balance sheet (cash, current assets, total assets, total liabilities and equity), before the 2021 SPAC merger; they do not affect a conclusion. Because one survival rule fails, the status is stopped at step 1. The analysis continues so that you can learn from it.

drivers.text: Interest coverage is -8.64, below the policy minimum of 5, because the company has operating losses.
drivers.reversing_change: Positive operating income above five times the interest expense would make the rule pass.

drivers.text: Net cash of more than $1 billion means that the risk of default in the near term is low, although the rule fails.
drivers.reversing_change: A large new debt issue, or cash use that removes the net cash position, would make the survival risk real.

steps.reason: Return on invested capital (ROIC, card roic: profit after tax from operations divided by the money invested in the business) was negative in every year; in 2025 it was -49.8% against a 9% WACC (card wacc: the minimum return that investors require). The rule of 7 years above WACC is not testable with 6 years, but no year passes. Gross margin increased from -3.0% in 2021 to 34.4% in 2025, which shows better unit economics. Operating margin is still -38.0%, because research and development for Neutron increased. Owner earnings (card owner-earnings: the cash that the owners can take out without harm to the business) were negative. Customer concentration is high: the top five customers gave about 49% of 2025 revenue, and U.S. government contracts gave about 47%. Space launch is a competitive market with a much larger competitor (SpaceX); the filings do not quantify market share. Score 2: the growth is fast, but the data does not show a profitable business yet.

steps.reason: Dilution (card dilution: an increase in the share count that makes each share own less of the company) is the main management issue. Diluted average shares increased from 466.2 million in 2022 to 530.7 million in 2025, and 7.0% in 2025 only; the cover-page count was 598.4 million on 2026-08-05. The company paid no dividends and made no buybacks. SBC fell from 52.3% of revenue in 2021 to 11.8% in 2025, which is better, but it is still high. Acquisitions used $132.4 million of cash in 2025, and goodwill increased from $71.0 million to $205.8 million; the data has no return for each acquisition. The cash raised by share issues pays for Neutron and acquisitions; this is reasonable for a company in this phase, but each owner's share decreases. Pay metrics are in proxy_pay.txt; this analysis did not score them. Score 2: high and continuing dilution with no return on capital yet.

steps.reason: The FCFF DCF (card fcff) is not meaningful because free cash flow to the firm was negative. For this reason the analysis uses a reverse DCF on revenue (card reverse-dcf): which revenue in year 10 makes the price correct? The assumptions are WACC 9%, terminal growth 2.5%, and a target free cash flow margin of 15%. The 15% target is an estimate: it is a mature margin for an aerospace manufacturer with high R&D, and it is higher than any margin that Rocket Lab has shown. With these assumptions the price requires year-10 revenue of $38.49 billion, against 2025 revenue of $601.8 million. That is 51.6% growth each year for ten years. This result is conditional on the start cash flow, the WACC, the terminal growth, the capital claims and the horizon. The floors are low: tangible book value is $2.16 per share and NCAV is $1.275 per share, against a price of $68.21. The market cap is $40.81 billion.

drivers.text: The price requires revenue to grow about 51.6% each year for ten years to $38.49 billion, with a 15% FCF margin.
drivers.reversing_change: A higher sustained FCF margin (for example from Neutron or a constellation business) would decrease the required revenue.

drivers.text: The asset floor ($2.16 tangible book value per share) gives almost no protection at $68.21.
drivers.reversing_change: None in the near term; the value depends on future cash flow, not on assets.

open_questions: Is 15% the right mature FCF margin for Rocket Lab, or do you want to test 10% and 20%?

steps.title: Commitment
steps.reason: Draft invalidation conditions: (1) revenue growth falls below 20% in a full year; (2) gross margin falls below 30% for two years; (3) diluted shares increase more than 5% in a year without positive free cash flow; (4) Neutron does not complete a first launch by the end of 2027; (5) cash and short-term investments fall below $1 billion. Pre-mortem: three years later the investment lost money because Neutron was late or failed, because a larger competitor decreased launch prices, because government contracts were delayed, or because new share issues decreased the value of each share. The price paid also assumed a growth rate that few companies achieve for ten years.

drivers.text: The thesis depends on Neutron and on the space systems business.
drivers.reversing_change: A successful Neutron start and positive free cash flow would decrease the risk.
